title: Notes from the field: rotavirus vaccine administration errors--United States, 2006-2013.
ehr_evidence: CDC searched for reports to the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) (2) of rotavirus vaccine administration errors involving injection and eye splashes in the United States during the period January 1, 2006–August 1, 2013.
summary: Analysis of 66 VAERS reports on rotavirus vaccine administration errors (injection and eye splashes) in the US from 2006 to 2013.
key_findings: 66 total reports of rotavirus vaccine administration errors were identified.
39 reports involved administration by injection (33 for RV1, 6 for RV5).
19 of 39 injection reports (49%) documented an adverse event, most commonly irritability (7 cases) and injection site redness (5).
30 of 39 injection reports (77%) lacked an explanation for the error.
27 reports involved eye splashes, with 21 cases (78%) describing nonserious minor eye irritation.
population: infants and children in the United States, 2006–2013
limitations: passive surveillance system likely captures only a small fraction of errors
no denominator data to calculate error rates
